name: AI Research
summary: Labs ship frontier models every month or two, driven by RL-trained reasoning, large compute buildouts and agents; safety, interpretability and evals work to keep up as benchmarks saturate.

regions.name: Pretraining & scaling
regions.summary: Frontier labs keep growing training compute and ship new flagships every month or two, with the most capable tiers often gated at first. Public training-compute data for closed models is sparse.

landmarks.name: Grok 4: largest known training run
landmarks.summary: Epoch AI estimates xAI's Grok 4 used about 5e26 FLOP, the largest training run in its data, with significant uncertainty because the estimate rests on vague xAI statements.

landmarks.name: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Astra
landmarks.summary: OpenAI's system card calls Astra its first model at the Critical cyber capability level. GPT-6 Sol and Luna followed in September and GPT-6 reached all ChatGPT users on 7 October.

landmarks.name: Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon
landmarks.summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Argon on 30 September and Carbon on 28 October, each going first to trusted cyber defenders through its Fairwind Program before any broad release.

landmarks.name: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
landmarks.summary: Anthropic upgraded its top tier: one underlying model sold as Fable (available to all, with cyber and biology safeguards) and Mythos (vetted organizations only).

regions.whyItMatters: Training scale still sets the ceiling for every downstream capability, and it drives the industry's spending.
regions.openQuestion: Do returns to larger training runs hold, or do gains now come mostly from RL, data and inference-time compute?

deepDives.title: Training compute of frontier AI models grows by 4-5x per year
deepDives.why: Epoch AI's baseline analysis of how fast training runs have scaled since 2010.

deepDives.title: Can AI scaling continue through 2030?
deepDives.why: Examines power, chips, data and latency as possible limits on further scaling.

deepDives.title: How many AI models will exceed compute thresholds?
deepDives.why: Epoch AI's counts and projections of models above given training-compute thresholds.

deepDives.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
deepDives.why: The 2020 paper relating loss to model size, data and compute that framed the scaling debate.

regions.name: Reasoning & reinforcement learning
regions.summary: RL on verifiable tasks plus test-time compute is the main driver of capability gains. Open recipes now reach olympiad-level math with small active parameter counts.

landmarks.name: DeepSeek-R1 paper revised
landmarks.summary: The paper that popularized RL-trained reasoning in open models was revised on arXiv in January 2026 and remains a reference point for open reasoning models.

landmarks.name: SU-01 open olympiad recipe
landmarks.summary: A 30B-A3B model trained with SFT, 200 RL steps and test-time scaling reaches gold-medal level on IMO 2025 and USAMO 2026 problems, plus physics olympiads.

landmarks.name: Microsoft MAI-Thinking-1 report
landmarks.summary: Microsoft AI describes a 35B-active, 1T-total MoE reasoning model trained from scratch, with RL runs of many thousands of steps on STEM and agentic coding tasks.

landmarks.name: Nemotron reaches IMO 2026 gold line
landmarks.summary: NVIDIA researchers report an open natural-language pipeline on Nemotron 3 Ultra scored 30 of 42 at IMO 2026, with checkpoints, data and code released.
landmarks.note: Self-reported score; abstract read via the Hugging Face paper page.

regions.whyItMatters: RL on checkable tasks is the main source of recent capability gains and is now reproducible outside the top labs.
regions.openQuestion: How far does RL on verifiable tasks transfer to open-ended work with no automatic checker?

deepDives.title: ARC Prize
deepDives.why: Benchmarks and leaderboards for novel reasoning tasks that models still find hard.

deepDives.title: FrontierMath
deepDives.why: Epoch AI's benchmark of advanced and research-level mathematics problems.

deepDives.title: DeepSeek-R1 incentivizes reasoning in LLMs through reinforcement learning
deepDives.why: Peer-reviewed version of the paper behind open RL-trained reasoning models.

deepDives.title: Spinning Up in Deep RL
deepDives.why: Free introduction to reinforcement learning concepts and core algorithms.

regions.name: Interpretability
regions.summary: Circuit tracing and sparse features now map parts of production models' internal computation. Work is shifting toward methods that put internal states into natural language, and toward open tooling.

landmarks.name: Circuit tracing with attribution graphs
landmarks.summary: Anthropic published a method for tracing step-by-step computation through a replacement model, with a companion study applying it to Claude 3.5 Haiku.

landmarks.name: Gemma Scope 2 released
landmarks.summary: Google DeepMind released open interpretability tools for all Gemma 3 sizes from 270M to 27B parameters, which it called the largest open release of its kind by an AI lab.

landmarks.name: Emotion concepts in Sonnet 4.5
landmarks.summary: Anthropic reported internal representations of emotion concepts in Claude Sonnet 4.5 that causally influence its outputs.

landmarks.name: Natural Language Autoencoders
landmarks.summary: Anthropic introduced an unsupervised method in which Claude is trained to translate its internal activations into natural-language explanations.

regions.whyItMatters: Reading a model's internals is one of the few ways to check what it is doing beyond its outputs.
regions.openQuestion: Can interpretability methods scale to give reliable, complete accounts of frontier model behavior?

deepDives.title: Open Problems in Mechanistic Interpretability
deepDives.why: Multi-lab 2025 review of what the field can and cannot yet do.

deepDives.title: Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits
deepDives.why: The essay that set out the circuits approach to reading neural networks.

deepDives.title: Neuronpedia
deepDives.why: Open source platform to explore, visualize and steer model internals.

deepDives.title: Transformer Circuits Thread
deepDives.why: Anthropic's running series of interpretability papers and monthly updates.

regions.name: Alignment & safety
regions.summary: Pre-deployment testing for scheming and dangerous capabilities is routine at top labs, but models increasingly recognize tests. Some capabilities are now gated rather than released.

landmarks.name: International AI Safety Report 2026
landmarks.summary: Second edition, led by Yoshua Bengio and written by over 100 experts with backing from over 30 countries and bodies, reviews AI capabilities, risks and risk management.

landmarks.name: Claude Mythos Preview gated
landmarks.summary: Anthropic kept Claude Mythos Preview as a gated research preview for Project Glasswing partners after saying it had identified thousands of zero-day vulnerabilities.

landmarks.name: Apollo: a science of scheming
landmarks.summary: Apollo Research argues scheming needs its own science of causes, and says the capabilities that enable evaluation, such as evaluation awareness, also make it harder.

landmarks.name: OpenAI and Apollo anti-scheming work
landmarks.summary: Across 26 out-of-distribution evaluations, deliberative alignment cut o3's covert action rate from 13% to 0.4%, but awareness of being evaluated may explain part of the drop.

regions.whyItMatters: Whether labs can detect and prevent misaligned behavior decides how safely more capable models can be deployed.
regions.openQuestion: Can evaluations stay informative once models reliably recognize when they are being tested?

deepDives.title: Frontier AI Trends Report
deepDives.why: UK AI Security Institute's evidence on frontier capabilities and safeguards from its testing.

deepDives.title: OpenAI Deployment Safety Hub
deepDives.why: OpenAI's system cards and addenda with safety evaluation results for each deployed model.

deepDives.title: Concrete Problems in AI Safety
deepDives.why: The 2016 paper that set out practical research problems such as reward hacking and safe exploration.

deepDives.title: AI Alignment Forum
deepDives.why: Where alignment researchers post and debate technical work.

regions.name: Evals & benchmarks
regions.summary: Classic benchmarks saturate quickly. Attention has moved to long-horizon task measures and novel interactive tests where models still score near zero.

landmarks.name: ARC-AGI-3 launches
landmarks.summary: Interactive, turn-based benchmark in which humans solve 100% of environments while frontier AI systems scored below 1% as of March 2026.

landmarks.name: METR Time Horizon 1.1
landmarks.summary: METR re-estimated model time horizons with a larger task suite, raising the number of tasks that take humans 8 or more hours from 14 to 31, and moved to the Inspect framework.

landmarks.name: METR time-horizon suite hits its ceiling
landmarks.summary: METR warned in May that measurements above 16 hours are unreliable with its current task suite, and in September said its time-horizons page is no longer actively updated.

regions.whyItMatters: Benchmarks shape how progress is perceived, and saturated ones hide what models can and cannot do.
regions.openQuestion: How can long, open-ended task ability be measured once fixed task suites saturate?

deepDives.title: Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models
deepDives.why: METR's measurements of how long a task models can complete, with methods and caveats.

deepDives.title: SWE-bench
deepDives.why: Leaderboards for resolving real GitHub issues, a standard coding-agent test.

deepDives.title: LMArena
deepDives.why: Crowd-voted head-to-head model rankings across text, vision and code.

deepDives.title: AI Index Report
deepDives.why: Stanford's annual reference on benchmark trends, investment and adoption.

regions.name: Efficiency, chips & inference
regions.summary: Inference demand from agents drives chip and data center spending. New GPU and TPU generations are ramping while open models cut long-context memory costs sharply.

landmarks.name: Nvidia Vera Rubin enters full production
landmarks.summary: Nvidia said at GTC Taipei that its Vera Rubin platform was ramping into full production, with shipments due from autumn and a claimed 10x agent throughput over Grace Blackwell.

landmarks.name: DeepSeek V4 open weights
landmarks.summary: Open-weights preview with a 1.6T-parameter MoE Pro model, a 1M-token context and compressed attention that DeepSeek says cuts memory use about 10x versus V3.2, at low API prices.

landmarks.name: Anthropic and Google TPU deal
landmarks.summary: Anthropic said it would use up to one million Google Cloud TPUs, worth tens of billions of dollars, with well over a gigawatt of capacity coming online in 2026.

regions.whyItMatters: Compute supply and cost per token decide who can train frontier models and what agents are affordable to run.
regions.openQuestion: Will inference demand keep pace with the chip and data center capacity now being built?

deepDives.title: Introducing the Frontier Data Centers Hub
deepDives.why: Epoch AI's tracker of the largest AI data centers, their power and compute capacity.

deepDives.title: MLPerf Inference: Datacenter
deepDives.why: Industry-standard benchmark results for inference hardware and systems.

deepDives.title: Data on machine learning hardware
deepDives.why: Epoch AI's dataset of AI chips with performance and price trends.

deepDives.title: AI chip users documentation: Methodology
deepDives.why: How Epoch estimates which companies hold how much AI compute.

regions.name: Multimodal & world models
regions.summary: Video models now generate synced audio, and interactive world models generate explorable environments used for simulation and robot training.

landmarks.name: Project Genie opens to users
landmarks.summary: Google released an experimental prototype powered by Genie 3 that lets US Google AI Ultra subscribers create, explore and remix interactive generated worlds.

landmarks.name: Waymo World Model built on Genie 3
landmarks.summary: Waymo described a driving simulator built on Genie 3 that generates rare events, such as a tornado, that are almost impossible to capture at scale in reality.

landmarks.name: Sora 2 with synchronized audio
landmarks.summary: OpenAI's video model generates synchronized dialogue and sound with video and launched alongside a social iOS app built around user likeness cameos.
landmarks.note: Trade press report; OpenAI's own page blocks automated reading.

regions.whyItMatters: Video and world models extend AI from text to simulation, media and training data for robots.
regions.openQuestion: Do generated worlds stay consistent enough to train agents and robots that work in reality?

deepDives.title: World Models
deepDives.why: The 2018 Ha and Schmidhuber paper on learning a generative model of an environment.

deepDives.title: Video generation models as world simulators
deepDives.why: OpenAI's technical note arguing video models learn physical regularities.

deepDives.title: Genie (Google DeepMind)
deepDives.why: Lab page for the Genie world models, with capabilities and stated limitations.

deepDives.title: Artificial Analysis
deepDives.why: Independent comparisons of language, image, video and speech models.

regions.name: Agent architectures, memory & tool use
regions.summary: Tool-use standards like MCP are now shared infrastructure under a neutral foundation. Persistent memory and continual learning for long-running agents remain open problems.

landmarks.name: Agent Skills joins Agentic AI Foundation
landmarks.summary: Anthropic donated the Agent Skills standard to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation, which it co-founded with Block and OpenAI in 2025 and which already hosts MCP.

landmarks.name: MCP 2026-07-28 spec goes stateless
landmarks.summary: The Model Context Protocol dropped its handshake and sessions for a stateless core, so any request can land on any server instance behind a plain load balancer.

landmarks.name: Memory-centric continual learning
landmarks.summary: Paper argues agent memory should be judged by whether it improves future actions, and models how performance scales with experience, storage and compute.

regions.whyItMatters: Shared protocols and memory decide whether agents can work across tools and improve over long tasks.
regions.openQuestion: How should long-running agents store and reuse experience without retraining the underlying model?

deepDives.title: Building effective agents
deepDives.why: Practical guide to agent patterns and when simpler workflows are enough.

deepDives.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
deepDives.why: The 2022 paper behind the reason-then-act loop most tool-using agents follow.

deepDives.title: Model Context Protocol specification
deepDives.why: The current protocol text for connecting models to tools and data.

deepDives.title: Agentic AI Foundation
deepDives.why: Linux Foundation home for MCP, Agent Skills and related open agent standards.

regions.name: Embodied AI & robotics
regions.summary: Vision-language-action models now control full humanoid bodies and several robot types from one model. Factories for home humanoids have opened, but real deployments remain small.

landmarks.name: Gemini Robotics 2
landmarks.summary: Google DeepMind's model controls entire humanoid bodies and ran three embodiments from one checkpoint, including Apptronik's Apollo 2; it is limited to early-access partners.

landmarks.name: 1X opens NEO humanoid factory
landmarks.summary: 1X opened a factory in Hayward, California for its NEO home humanoid with capacity for 10,000 units in year one; early units go to internal testing before customer deliveries.

landmarks.name: Physical Intelligence opens API beta
landmarks.summary: The robot foundation model lab made its latest models available for fine-tuning and cloud-hosted inference on customers' own robots through a Pi API beta.

regions.whyItMatters: Robotics tests whether foundation-model progress carries over to physical work.
regions.openQuestion: Can general robot models reach the reliability needed for unsupervised use in homes and factories?

deepDives.title: Open X-Embodiment: Robotic Learning Datasets and RT-X Models
deepDives.why: Cross-lab robot dataset and models that started the generalist-policy push.

deepDives.title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models
deepDives.why: Showed web-scale vision-language models can output robot actions.

deepDives.title: Hugging Face Robotics Course
deepDives.why: Free hands-on course on robot learning with open tools and datasets.

deepDives.title: Physical Intelligence blog
deepDives.why: Research notes from one of the main generalist robot policy labs.

deepDives.title: Training compute of frontier AI models grows by 4-5x per year
deepDives.why: Data-driven account of how fast frontier training runs are growing.

deepDives.title: AI Index Report
deepDives.why: Stanford's annual reference on technical progress, investment and adoption.

deepDives.title: Import AI
deepDives.why: Jack Clark's weekly newsletter summarizing notable AI research.

deepDives.title: Anthropic research
deepDives.why: Primary source for Anthropic's alignment, interpretability and societal impact work.

deepDives.title: Google DeepMind model cards
deepDives.why: Official cards for current Google models, with intended use and evaluation results.
